en.name: Conger eel
en.summary: Conger eel, anago, is the lean saltwater eel of sushi counters and tempura, sold cleaned and split. Refrigerated it keeps 1–2 days; frozen, 6–8 months. It is always cooked, never eaten raw.
en.pantry: Conger does not keep at room temperature. It is also one of the fish that must be cooked: eel blood, conger's included, contains a toxin that makes raw eel unsafe, and it is destroyed by heat — which is why anago always arrives simmered, grilled or fried and never as sashimi. Bring it home cold, follow the 2-hour rule, or 1 hour above 32 °C (90 °F), and keep it below ready-to-eat food in the bag as well as in the fridge.
en.fridge: Buy it already killed, cleaned and split — that is how it is normally sold — and hold it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below on ice, in a container that catches the melt water, cooking it within 1–2 days. Lay the fillets skin side down on a rack rather than letting them sit in liquid. Conger flesh is soft and gelatinous and it loses body quickly; if you cannot cook it within a day, simmer it in a light broth and keep the cooked eel instead, which buys you a little more time as a cooked fish.
en.freezer: Conger keeps 6–8 months at −18 °C (0 °F) — much longer than freshwater eel, because it is far leaner and there is less fat to oxidise. Wrap the split fillets tightly with no air pockets, or ice-glaze them, and freeze flat in portions. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are a quality window. Cooked, sauced anago freezes well too and is often the more useful thing to have in the freezer.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge overnight on a plate, or in a sealed bag under cold running water. Never on the counter or in warm water. Cook it through promptly and do not refreeze raw eel.
spoilage: A sour or ammoniacal smell instead of a clean sea one.
Flesh that has gone soft and will not spring back when pressed.
A slimy, sticky surface or cloudy liquid pooling under the fillet.
A grey or yellow cast where the flesh should be pale and pearly.
tips: Buy it cleaned and split; conger is awkward to dress at home.
Keep it on a rack over ice, not in the melt water.
Cook it through — eel is never eaten raw.
If in doubt, simmer it today and refrigerate the cooked eel instead.

faq.q: How long does fresh conger eel keep?
faq.a: 1–2 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, on ice. Frozen, 6–8 months at −18 °C.

faq.q: Can you eat conger eel raw?
faq.a: No. Eel blood contains a heat-sensitive toxin, so anago is always cooked — simmered, grilled or fried.

faq.q: Why does conger freeze longer than unagi?
faq.a: It is much leaner. Fat is what oxidises in the freezer, so a lean eel holds its quality far longer than a fatty freshwater one.

faq.q: How can you tell if conger has gone off?
faq.a: A sour or ammoniacal smell, slime on the surface, or flesh that stays dented when pressed.

zh.name: 星鰻
zh.summary: 星鰻（穴子）是壽司店和天婦羅常用的低脂海水鰻，通常已經剖開清理好才販售。冷藏可放 1～2 天，冷凍 6～8 個月。它一律要煮熟，絕不生食。
zh.pantry: 星鰻不能放室溫。它同時也是必須煮熟的魚之一：鰻魚的血（星鰻也一樣）含有毒素，使生鰻不適合食用，而這種毒素會被加熱破壞——這就是為什麼穴子總是以滷煮、燒烤或油炸的形式出現，從來不做成生魚片。請保冷帶回家，守 2 小時原則（室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時），在提袋裡和冰箱裡都放在即食食品的下方。
zh.fridge: 請買已經宰殺、清理、剖開的（市面上本來就多半這樣賣），鋪冰放 4 °C 以下，容器要能接住融水，並在 1～2 天內煮掉。魚片皮朝下放在網架上，不要泡在滲出的液體裡。星鰻肉質軟嫩帶膠質，很快就會失去彈性；如果一天內煮不到，可以先用淡味高湯滷過，改成保存「煮熟的星鰻」，那樣可以照熟魚的規格多撐一點時間。
zh.freezer: 星鰻在 −18 °C 下可放 6～8 個月——比淡水鰻長得多，因為它瘦得多，可氧化的脂肪少。剖開的魚片包緊不留空氣，或做冰鍍，分裝壓平冷凍。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質。做成蒲燒醬味的熟星鰻也很耐凍，通常放在冷凍庫裡更實用。
zh.thawing: 放盤子上冷藏隔夜解凍，或密封裝袋用冷水沖。不要放室溫或泡溫水。解凍後盡快煮透，生鰻不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸或有氨味，而不是乾淨的海味。
魚肉變軟，按壓後回不來。
表面黏滑，或魚片下方積出混濁液體。
本該淡白帶珍珠光澤的魚肉泛灰或泛黃。
tips: 買清理剖開好的；星鰻在家處理很麻煩。
架在網架上放冰的上方，不要泡在融水裡。
一定要煮熟——鰻魚不生食。
拿不準的話，今天先滷過，改存熟的。

faq.a: 鋪冰放 4 °C 以下 1～2 天。冷凍則是 −18 °C 下 6～8 個月。
不行。鰻魚血含有不耐熱的毒素，所以穴子一律煮熟——滷煮、燒烤或油炸。

faq.q: 星鰻為什麼比鰻魚（白鰻）耐凍？
faq.a: 因為它瘦得多。冷凍庫裡會變質的是脂肪，所以低脂的鰻種品質維持得久很多。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷星鰻不新鮮了？
faq.a: 發酸或氨味、表面黏滑，或按壓後凹陷回不來。
